summary.name: Go for SREs Using Python
summary.one_liner: A SREcon16 slide deck by Andrew Hamilton comparing the Go programming language with Python for site reliability engineering work.
use_cases: Deciding whether to write SRE tooling in Go or Python
Building a CLI tool or API quickly for operations work
Distributing a single self-contained binary to hosts without dependency setup
Understanding Go concurrency with goroutines and channels
Learning Go's toolchain, testing and error-handling conventions as a Python developer
summary.what_it_does: The slides describe Go's strengths for SRE work: a fast, statically typed, compiled language with a standard library that covers most needs, built-in concurrency via goroutines and channels, and a default toolchain including gofmt, go test, go vet and a race detector. They contrast Go's error-return style with Python's exceptions and explain godoc for offline documentation. They also cover dependency handling, noting Go has no PyPI equivalent and that dependencies are vendored within the project. The main argument is that Go produces a single binary, which avoids the pip and virtualenv problems seen during 2am incidents.
notable: Compiles to a single self-contained binary with cross-compilation support
Built-in goroutines and channels for concurrency
Vendoring for dependency versioning; no PyPI equivalent
Notes there is no official Go debugger, only unofficial ones
caveats: No official debugger for Go as of the talk
Third-party dependencies are local to $GOPATH and there is no central package registry like PyPI
Presentation from 2016; tooling details may be outdated
